problem:
Find the center and radius of the osculating circle to the curve $r(t)$ at the point $P(0,0)$ where $t=0,$ given that $‖{r}^{′}(0)‖=1,$ and the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ to the curve is

$$
T(t)=⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩.
$$
worked_solution:
Since we are given both the value of $‖{r}^{′}(0)‖$ and the unit tangent $T(t)$, we will use the following formula for the radius of curvature:

$$
R(t)=\frac{1}{κ(t)}=\frac{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

Notice that $r(0)=⟨0,0⟩,$ since the point $P(0,0)$ is at the tip of $r(0).$ 

Now, we find ${T}^{′}(t)$, ${T}^{′}(0)$ and $‖{T}^{′}(0)‖:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩ \\ {T}^{′}(0) & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡0,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡0⟩ \\  & =⟨1,0⟩ \\ ‖{T}^{′}(0)‖ & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the radius of curvature is

$$
\begin{aligned}R(0) & =\frac{‖{r}^{′}(0)‖}{‖{T}^{′}(0)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{1} \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we find the principal normal vector at $t=0$ as

$$
\begin{aligned}N(0) & =\frac{{T}^{′}(0)}{‖{T}^{′}(0)‖}=⟨1,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the center of the osculating circle is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(0)+R(0)N(0) & =⟨0,0⟩+1\cdot ⟨1,0⟩ \\  & =⟨0,0⟩+⟨1,0⟩ \\  & =⟨1,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

choices.value: The center is $⟨1,0⟩$ and the radius is $1$
The center is $⟨0,-1⟩$ and the radius is $1$
The center is $⟨1,1⟩$ and the radius is $1$
The center is $⟨1,0⟩$ and the radius is $2$
The center is $⟨1,-1⟩$ and the radius is $2$
